title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand what icarKno is: an AI-powered document intelligence platform that lets users upload PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, CSV/XLSX and other formats, then query them with natural language using hybrid keyword+vector search, multi-step AI reasoning, and multi-language (23+ languages) support. The README also documents the architecture, project structure, and Docker-based deployment, giving you the roadmap this tour will walk through in code.

title: Application Entry Point
description: run.py is the literal starting point of the running system: it imports the Flask application factory and launches the dev server bound to 0.0.0.0:5001 in production mode. It has the lowest fan-in in the whole graph (nothing else depends on it) yet it is where execution begins, which is the classic signature of an entry point versus a library module.

title: The Application Factory
description: app/__init__.py is the module run.py actually calls into. It builds and configures the Flask app: setting up logging, loading environment-specific configuration via ConfigFactory, enabling CORS, initializing extensions, registering every API blueprint, and defining global JSON error handlers. This factory pattern is what wires together everything else you'll see in this tour -- the API layer, the config system, and the rate-limiting extensions.
languageLesson: The 'application factory' pattern (create_app()) lets Flask apps be instantiated multiple times with different configs -- essential for testing and for running dev/staging/production from the same codebase without global state leaking between instances.

title: Centralized Configuration
description: app/config.py is the second-most depended-upon file in the codebase (11 incoming references), meaning nearly every service and controller reads its settings. It defines a BaseConfig with environment-driven settings for Elasticsearch, MongoDB, MySQL, JWT, rate limiting, the GPU inference server, and Vexyl STT/TTS, plus Development/Testing/Production subclasses selected through a ConfigFactory. Pair this with .env.example, which documents every environment variable -- API keys, database credentials, and speech service settings -- that BaseConfig expects to find.
languageLesson: Python's class-inheritance config pattern (BaseConfig -> DevelopmentConfig/ProductionConfig) keeps shared defaults in one place while letting each environment override only what differs, avoiding scattered if-environment-equals checks throughout the codebase.

title: Document Upload and Container Management
description: app/api/documents.py is the Flask blueprint that implements the README's first feature: getting documents into the system. It exposes routes for free-trial uploads, authenticated file/URL uploads, file retrieval, and container (session) renaming/listing/deletion. Every route delegates real work to document_service.py, keeping the blueprint itself thin -- a pattern you'll see repeated across the API layer.

title: Document Processing Pipeline
description: document_service.py has the highest fan-out in the entire codebase (8 outgoing dependencies), making it the busiest orchestrator: it classifies uploaded files by type, routes them to document, data, or URL processing pipelines, and manages the lifecycle of each user's document container. file_storage_service.py handles the actual on-disk persistence of those files per session, and url_content_service.py extracts content from arbitrary web pages and YouTube videos so they can be ingested the same way as uploaded files.

title: Text Extraction and Chunking
description: Once document_service.py knows what kind of file it has, utils/extractText.py does the heavy lifting: pulling clean text out of PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and TXT files, converting tables to markdown, and tracking page/table metadata. controllers/upload.py then takes that raw text and produces hierarchical, markdown-aware chunks -- the unit of retrieval that Elasticsearch will later search over. This is the 'intelligent chunking' the README promises for optimal retrieval.

title: Elasticsearch: Index and Storage
description: With chunks in hand, three elastic/ modules persist them for search. elastic/client.py is a singleton wrapper around the shared Elasticsearch connection; elastic/index_manager.py creates and manages the index itself using a custom mapping with dense_vector embeddings plus Hindi/multilingual text analyzers; and elastic/document_manager.py stores the chunked documents with embeddings, applying Unicode/Hindi-aware preprocessing before indexing. Together these three implement the storage half of the README's 'hybrid search' feature.

title: Hybrid Retrieval
description: elastic/retriever.py is the read-side counterpart to Step 8's write-side storage: it implements hybrid keyword+vector retrieval using an EnsembleRetriever, with LLM-based query enrichment that rewrites queries using chat context before searching, plus a helper for fetching every chunk belonging to a specific table. This is what the README calls 'Hybrid Search: Combines keyword and vector search for best results.'

title: The LLM Service Hub
description: app/services/llm_service.py has by far the highest fan-in in the codebase (13 incoming dependencies) -- nearly every reasoning, search, and synthesis service you'll meet next calls into it. It defines a custom LangChain-compatible chat model that talks to a self-hosted GPU inference server, and exposes factory functions for differently-tuned LLM instances (fast, standard, comprehensive, creative, code, streaming). This hub-and-spoke shape is exactly what you'd expect from a shared infrastructure dependency: everything needs an LLM, so everything imports this one module.
languageLesson: Factory functions like get_fast_llm()/get_creative_llm() that all funnel through a private _make_llm() helper are a common way to expose multiple pre-configured variants of an expensive object without duplicating construction logic.

title: Multi-Step Reasoning Pipeline
description: This cluster of services implements the README's 'Creative Reasoning: Advanced multi-step analysis for complex queries.' reasoning_strategy_service.py decomposes a query into a structured multi-step search strategy; search_execution_service.py executes that strategy by building a dependency-ordered plan and running document/SQL/summary/hybrid searches through context_provider_service.py (which centralizes retrieval across Elasticsearch, the SQL database, and the summarizer); adaptive_search_service.py iteratively refines queries across rounds using result_evaluation_service.py's LLM-based sufficiency judgments; and result_synthesis_service.py formats everything with citations into a final structured, streamable answer. creative_reasoning_service.py ties all of this together as the orchestrator for open-ended queries.

title: Structured Data: SQL and Summarization
description: Not every query is about unstructured text. controllers/sql_db.py manages per-session SQLite databases created from uploaded CSV/Excel files, converting natural-language questions into SQL via an LLM chain and executing them safely -- this is the README's 'SQL Generation: Automatic conversion of questions to database queries' feature. controllers/doc_summary.py complements it with extractive (BERT-based) and LLM-driven abstractive summarization across a session's uploaded files. Both are part of the older controllers/ layer that predates the app/api blueprint structure, but context_provider_service.py from Step 11 calls directly into them, showing how the new service layer wraps rather than replaces this legacy code.

title: The Query Pipeline and Chat API
description: app/api/queries.py is the second-busiest API file (6 outgoing dependencies) and the largest blueprint in the project: it powers trial/authenticated Q&A (sync and streaming), image captioning, chat history, notes, and demo queries. Every request flows through query_agent_service.py, the top-level orchestrator that combines intent classification (query_intent_service.py), chat context retrieval, and the reasoning pipeline from Steps 10-11 into a single process_query call, while response_generator_service.py builds the final mode-specific prompt and translates the answer into the user's requested language. chat_models.py defines the ChatMessage/ChatSession/ChatContext data classes that flow through this entire pipeline, and chat_history_manager.py persists them to MongoDB.

title: Security, Translation, and Voice
description: Three utility-layer services support every query above. utils/guardrails.py is a SecurityPipeline that sanitizes input and detects prompt-injection attempts before a query is ever processed -- query_service.py applies these guardrails up front. utils/translation.py delegates to a remote IndicTrans2 server to translate between English and 23 Indic languages, implementing the README's multi-language support. app/services/stt_service.py and tts_service.py round out the README's voice features by connecting to an external Vexyl backend for speech-to-text and text-to-speech, both wired into app/api/queries.py's /stt and /tts routes from Step 13.

title: Accounts, Auth, and API Reference
description: Rounding out the platform, app/api/accounts.py and account_service.py implement subscription/payment plan management and login, backed by controllers/database.py's direct MongoDB functions for password hashing, JWT session creation, and rate limiting -- another example of the service layer delegating to the legacy controllers layer. To see how all of these pieces -- documents, queries, accounts, speech, and translation -- come together as a consumable REST surface, consult api-documentation.md, which documents every endpoint this tour has touched, including the WhatsApp webhook integration mentioned in the README.
